svg.title: From a commit to Cape Town
svg.desc: From a commit to Cape Town, in three lanes: Laptop, GitHub (KatlehoKomeke/Appointment-Booking-System) and AWS. Everything drawn is built. Step A, along the top: the administrator, branchbook-admin signed in with aws login, runs cdk deploy BranchbookAccount by hand with BRANCHBOOK_ALERT_EMAIL set. Laptop: step 1, git commit. Step 2, the pre-commit hook refuses .env files, keys, .claude/ and cdk.context.json, then runs gitleaks on the staged diff; it fails closed, and a refused edge leads to 'commit refused: a finding, or no scanner'. Step 3, the post-commit hook prints a reminder after a major commit and never blocks. A caveat note joined to both hooks: they are opt-in (make hooks), and --no-verify skips the pre-commit hook. Step 4, git push, the start of the main path, which crosses into GitHub. GitHub: a small file, aws-connection-check.yml, runs only by hand. Step 5, push protection refuses known provider secrets; a refused edge leads to 'push rejected'. Step 6, main, a gate: a push starts ci and secret-scan; a push or merge needs the required checks api, web, stack, infra and gitleaks, and a force-push is refused. Step 7, ci.yml: the jobs api, web, stack and infra run together with no AWS access. Four needs edges lead to step 8, the deploy job, which needs all four: it runs on an ARM runner, builds the ARM64 image natively, never runs on a pull request, and leaves with an OIDC token through the gate environment aws-demo, which admits main and v* tags only. Below ci.yml, secret-scan.yml, job gitleaks, scans the full history after the push; it cannot block a push, but its check is required to merge. AWS: step 9, AWS STS, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, returns credentials for at most 1 h; a dotted line joins STS to the role's trust policy. In AWS · us-east-1 (N. Virginia), the BranchbookAccount stack holds the IAM OIDC provider GitHubOidcProvider and the IAM role branchbook-github-deploy, whose trust policy requires aud and sub to match; IAM is global, so the stack lives in us-east-1, and it also holds the cost budget. In AWS · af-south-1 (Cape Town): step 10, the CDK bootstrap roles file-publishing, image-publishing and deploy; the image is pushed to ECR. Step 11, AWS CloudFormation, as the cfn-exec role, deploys BranchbookData, the network and the database, then BranchbookApp, WAF, the load balancer and the task; both are built by the pipeline. Step 12, on the edge to the next stack, the job smoke-tests branchbook.click. Step 13, the BranchbookRelease stack, which the same job deploys, highlighted, records /branchbook/release = GITHUB_SHA. Step 14, the main path returns to GitHub: the job reads /branchbook/release back, and it must equal GITHUB_SHA, or the job fails. Last in GitHub, Dependabot opens weekly pull requests; ci and secret-scan run on them, and deploy never does. Legend: Built; Main path; Refused or not allowed; Gap or caveat; AWS category: security, management and integration.
